# Pip v4: build guide (generated by `python -m rnd.build_guide`)

**First build:** about **24 h hands-on** (ESTIMATE), plus about **354 h of unattended P2S printing** (14.8 kg PETG/ASA). Reconfiguring later: an arm cartridge swap is 4 ear screws (M4 + nuts) with the belt on (~3 min); an arm comes off with one V-band clamp.
**One arm** (the first milestone build): about **6.2 h** hands-on (6.18 → 6.18 h, +0 min, since the last guide), plus ≈ 78 h of printing.

Parts: [BOM](rnd/BOM_v4.md) · M1 kit: [M1_BENCH_ARM.md](M1_BENCH_ARM.md) · prints: [print plan](rnd/print_plan.md) · wiring: [electrical](rnd/electrical.md) · checks: [assembly](rnd/assembly.md), [sim](rnd/sim.md)

| Step | What | Count | Min each | Hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 Coupons | Print + test the Step-1 coupons (COUPONS.md): C9 GIM bolt circles, C12 insert pull-out (M3 / M4 inserts in 3 mm bosses), C13 4-ear flange (M4 × 12 + washers into captive nuts, centring lip: 16.5 N·m proof, tipping, 72 h at 50 °C), C14 drive stub (the GIM output's tilt, PCD and pilot; 8 × M3 × 6 + Loctite 243 to 1.5 × the 11 N·m peak on a dummy output); measure the printed C1 / rear-mount stacks and order or face the crush sleeves to print − 0.05 mm; adjust the flange / bolt circles in rnd/parts before mass printing | 1 | 60 | 1.0 |
| 3 KX sockets | D15 screwed socket, head pan + tilt only (D24: the arm has none; lift v2 bolts): 6 dowels, 6 coil springs, collar, retainer (3 × M3 into inserts); 3 balls into the male face with retaining compound | 2 | 8 | 0.3 |
| 4a Bolted cartridges | D24 v2: 2 × M3 heat-set inserts in the sleeve lugs; motor into the sleeve from the rear, rear cap (3 × DIN 7984 M3 × 8 to the motor + 2 × M3 × 10 into the lugs); D26 integral pinion shaft (stub v5, the 20T hobbed on it: no key, no pulley) on the output (8 × DIN 7984 M3 × 6, Loctite 243), 6001 (lift: 61901) pressed on its k5 seat; label + CAN ID (pitch, yaw, elbow × 2 + lift) | 7 | 9 | 1.1 |
| 4b Wrist cartridges | D24: DM-J4310 into its can, bolted can flange and output flange (inserts + 6 × M3 each); label + CAN ID | 2 | 9 | 0.3 |

| 5b Clock springs | Wind the 6 ribbon cassettes per arm (D14 ribbon) and fit them at pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist pitch, wrist roll | 2 | 30 | 1.0 |

| 8 Mast + torso + head | Ratchet strip segments, lift drive + belt, carriage (8 × 625), torso halves around the carriage, head bracket + pan/tilt + shell | 1 | 150 | 2.5 |
| 9 Base | 4 wheel modules (pods, shafts, hubs, wheels), deck quarters, skirt, coupling, battery bay, lidar, electronics; 4 D18b casters (rods, lock plate, spring, 24 V solenoid) into their guides, 2 ballast stacks bolted and dropped into their cradles (W8d) | 1 | 150 | 2.5 |
| 10 Wiring | Pre-made daisy-chain harness segments (JST-GH CAN/TTL, VH power) per module; power distribution board; detach plugs | 1 | 120 | 2.0 |

| | **Total hands-on** | | | **24.3** |

**Wave 1 (D24 bolted cartridges, D19):** sockets + cartridges 3.8 → 2.6 h for the robot; one arm 6.05 → 6.18 h (+8 min). The 5 D15 sockets per arm go (−40 min); the bolted cartridges' inserts and Oldham hub take about half of that back. D19's one-piece shaft-pulleys replace the split pulleys (no keyed joint to fit) at about the same time, the seat-cap screws included.

**Against R10** (first build ≤ 4 h): **not met.**
- **Loop 10 cut the estimate from 25 h to ~19 h:**
    - print-in-place KX sockets with pins and spring embedded at print pauses (no retainer, no screws) — *retired in loop 40 (D15): the screwed socket takes ≈ 8 min; D24 then removed the sockets from the arm*
    - 7 instead of 14 screws per cartridge
    - eccentric-bushing belt tensioning — *retired in D26: fixed centres, a slotted idler at the pitch*
    - pre-made harness segments
- **A 21-actuator robot won't reach 4 h.** Precedent: a 6-servo LeRobot SO-101 arm takes a few hours.
- **Proposed target split (owner decision):** first build of one arm ≤ 4 h; whole robot ≤ 15 h; any module swap ≤ 5 min.

## Safety notes
- 24 V Li-ion: use the specified BMS (≥ 30 A), fuse every branch, and charge on a non-flammable surface.
- The arms can pinch. Torque limits are set in the drives (bring-up step 2, saved to flash) and bounded again by the safety supervisor. The bolted arm cartridges have **no mechanical slip backstop** (the KX seats slipped at ≈ 1.16× peak); only the head sockets still do.
- Test the lift pawl, the e-stop and the watchdog (sw/bringup.py step 3) before any powered arm motion; bench work with the catch cradle ≤ 50 mm under the arm.
